To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nucleotide binding to SERCA produces site-specific, yet counter-balancing effects, on backbone dynamics that propagate through the central, beta-sheet domain.
nucleotide binding has no effect on the global fold of the isolated N-domain of SERCA, but produces diverse effects on backbone dynamics, which converge on the central sheet domain.
the overall fold of SERCA-N was not affected by AMP-PNP binding, but that the dynamics of the central beta-sheet was modulated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural dynamics and conformational changes in the N domain of SERA, and the effects of nucleotides and Ca(2+).
the structural and dynamical properties of SERCA, which is a member of the P-type ATPase family of ion pumps, and the most extensively studied member of this family.
the structural basis of SERCA function, which is essential in maintaining the Ca2+ homeostasis in muscle and non-muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N domain of SERCAs is highly dynamic and nucleotide binding induces a variety of effects on the backbone motions, which may have implications for SERCA function.

the nucleotide-binding effects observed in the isolated N domain are likely to be transmitted to the intact SERCA molecule, and may be involved in modulating the dynamics of the actuator and phosphorylation domains, which in turn may influence the overall conformational changes of SERCA during the transport cycle.
the nucleotide-binding site in SERCA-N does not undergo major structural rearrangement in the absence of ATP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isolated N domain is a good model for the nucleotide-bound state of the intact SERCA.
the isolated N domain is a stable fold, with a well-defined core, that is largely independent of nucleotide binding, but which exhibits a dynamic interface between the N domain and the A domain.
the nucleotide-binding site in SERCA-N is highly dynamic, yet the global fold is stable, and that nucleotide binding has little effect on the stability of the domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nucleotide-binding effects are not readily manifested on SERCA-N global fold and stability, yet are manifested on backbone dynamics, with the effects propagating through the central beta-strand domain.
the nucleotide-binding site is a highly dynamic region of SERCA-N, with nucleotide binding having the potential to influence the dynamics of the central beta-sheet and the surrounding regions.

nucleotide binding to the N domain of SERCa does not affect its global fold and stability, but does produce site-specific effects on backbone dynamics, which are consistent with the notion of a dynamic equilibrium between the N domain and its ligand, which is essential for its function.
